sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 27.02.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 27.02.2021 at about 11.00 p.m., while petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-3047 on KKP-Maralavadi Road at Buduguppe cross, Kasaba hobli, Kanakapura taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time, one dog suddenly came across the road and to avoid the same, rider of the said motor cycle suddenly applied brake, and as a result, petitioner and rider thrown on the road and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Kanakapura Government hospital for first aid, thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.

It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was a student studying II PUC in Kanakapura Rural College and also doing agricultural work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-EA-3047.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has entered its appearance through its learned counsel.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absence, hence he was placed exparte.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.

Further it has admitted the issuance of package policy in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-EA-3047 from 08.01.2019 till 07.01.2024(one year for OD and 5 years to cover the risk of third party) and contended that on the date of alleged accident policy was not covering the risk of pillion rider of the offending motor cycle and the liability if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

The rider of the offending motor cycle was not holding valid driving license Jayaprakash vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145423748/
2 as on the date of the accident and therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 27.02.2021 at about 11.00 p.m., near KKP-Maralavadi Road, at Buduguppe cross, Kasaba hobli, Kanakapura taluk,
Ramanagara District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A- 3047?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P1 to 16.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has not led its defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ...

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  For the following:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 27.02.2021 at about 11.00 p.m., while petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-3047 on KKP-Maralavadi Road at Buduguppe cross, Kasaba hobli, Kanakapura taluk, Ramanagara District,
at that time, one dog suddenly came across the road and to avoid the same, rider of the said motor cycle suddenly applied brake, and as a result, petitioner and rider thrown on the road and sustained injuries.
The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the Jayaprakash vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024

Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 7.
11.
The accident said to have occurred on 27.02.2021 at 11.00 p.m.

The first information statement was lodged on 06.03.2021 at 5.40 p.m. by the mother of the injured clearly narrating the manner of the accident and the registration number of the offending motor cycle.
It is contended by the respondent that there is seven days delay in lodging the complaint.
However, in the FIS it is clearly mentioned that after providing treatment to her son, she has lodged the complaint belatedly.
When there is severe injury to any person, priority is to be given for medical aid to the injured and not to lodge first information.

Hence, even if there is a delay of seven days in lodging first information, it cannot be doubted since soon after the accident after providing first aid at Government hospital,
injured was taken to Sanjay Gandhi hospital and the cause of accident is also clearly mentioned in the Wound Certificate at Ex.P6.

Even in the cross examination of PW.1 it is elicited that since his leg was fractured and he was taking treatment in the hospital and his mother was looking after him,
they could not lodge complaint in time and there is delay.
The motor vehicles accident report produced at Ex.P5 shows the damages caused to the vehicle.
No explanation given by the respondent No.1 for the damages caused to the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-EA-3047.
The motor vehicles accident report shows the involvement of the said offending motor cycle in the accident.
12. It is the contention of the respondent No.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
There is no reason to distrust the evidence of PW1 with regard manner of the accident.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet at Ex.P7 against the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-42-EA-3047 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to the negligence or rider of the the motor cycle.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42- EA-3047.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-EA-3047.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was a II puc student and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show his income.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2021.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained fracture of medial malleolus left ankle and Jayaprakash vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145423748/
4 dento-alveolar fracture upper jaw.

sentences.text: Petitioner was treated with POP splint and medications.

On examination, the petitioner is facing difficulty in climbing stairs,
squatting, sitting cross legged and kneeling.
He assessed permanent physical impairment at 32% and 11% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 8% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 19 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 27.02.2021.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P10 Adhaar card as 27.02.2002, the petitioner was aged 19 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 19 is 18 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,59,200/-(Rs.15,000x12x18x8/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
Wound certificate produced at Ex.P6, reveals the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the doctor has opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
The Ex.P8 ER record of Sanjay Gandhi hospital reveals that petitioner took treatment in the said hospital on 28.02.2021.
Petitioner has suffered fracture of medial malleolus left ankle and dento-alveolar fracture upper jaw and two teeth are replaced.
The petitioner has taken conservative treatment and certainly he has undergone much pain and sufferings.

Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.20,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The discharge summaries of Ex.P8 ER record of Sanjay Gandhi hospital reveals that petitioner took treatment in the said hospital on 28.02.2021.
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.7,750/- as per Ex.P11 and 12.
I have examined the medical bills, payment receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.7,750/- and he is entitled for the same.

5 17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated in the hospital, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.

sentences.text: Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.3,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least one month.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.15,000/- (15,000 X 1) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 19 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 8% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- on this head.

20 . Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

sentences.text: Total Rs. Rs.3,24,950/-
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,24,950/-.
21. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-EA-3047.
Though in the written statement respondent No.1 has disputed with regard to the package policy issued to the offending vehicle, has not produced any supporting documents.
The breach of any of the policy conditions also are not proved.
It is not disputed that 1st respondent is the insurer and 2nd respondent is the owner.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,24,950/-(Rupees Three lakhs twenty four thousand nine hundred and fifty only) with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 60% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
